reason: The culm (stem) is 'brownish-tinged at base'. Stem base (PO_0008039) with brown fits. The tinge is weak, but the colour is right.
'Heads few-flowered' means there are few flowers in the head (capitulum). Flower present, inside an inflorescence container, with the count word 'few' says this.

target: lobe of the floral disc scale (FLOPO_0986025 as the whole; a general lobe class, not PO_0025517)
fix: When an 'N-lobed' count's container is not a leaf, the bearer must be a lobe of that container. Do not fall back to 'leaf lamina lobe'.
reason: The 7-10 lobes belong to the disk scale (floral disc), not to a leaf blade. The container is right, but the bearer is a leaf part.

target: position slot: towards the sapwood (outer heartwood); main colour yellowish brown
fix: In 'X with a Y tinge towards Z', Y is a secondary tinge that only occurs near Z. Keep the position, or annotate X as the main colour.
reason: The heartwood is yellowish brown. Only a tinge near the sapwood is reddish or pinkish. Saying the heartwood is red or pink, with no place given, is false.

fix: In '<colour> hirsute/pilose/pubescent', the colour belongs to the hairs, not to the part that carries them.
reason: 'Densely yellow hirsute' means the peduncle has yellow hairs. The peduncle itself is not said to be yellow.
'Style longer than the corolla': increased length of the style compared with the corolla is right.

target: alternatives brownish | olive (FLOPO_0988005) | yellowish green (PATO_0104114, sometimes), on the adaxial surface
fix: In a list 'A, B, or sometimes C', every member is an alternative. The value relation must not keep only the last pair. Keep the 'adaxially' surface slot too.
reason: The flora gives three colours: brownish, olive, or sometimes yellowish green. The annotation drops 'brownish' and also drops the adaxial surface.
Basal leaves (FLOPO_0991002) that are petiolate is right. The 'long' only adds degree.
'Bracts ... equal to calyx' compares length. Bract length at a 1:1 ratio to the calyx is right.
'Not much reduced' is the negation of 'greatly reduced'. The scope is right.

fix: A sex word in front of a part ('pistillate/staminate/male/female flowers') must go into the state slot. Here the staminate flowers are described separately.
reason: Only the pistillate flowers are said to be numerous. Without 'pistillate', the claim is about all flowers.
Plants 0.5-3 × 1-2 dm: the second dimension is the width. 1-2 dm = 10-20 cm is right.

target: place slot: bract base, for the pubescent alternative
fix: In 'A or B at base', the place phrase belongs to the alternative it follows. Keep the place on B, or substitute the bearer (bract base) for B.
reason: The bracts are either glabrous or pubescent at the base. Putting 'pubescent' on the whole bract states more than the flora says.

target: plant cell wall of the basal leaf cells (thickness)
fix: 'Incrassate' cells (common in mosses) means cells with thickened walls. The thickness belongs to the cell wall, not to the cell. 'Basal' (cells at the leaf base) should be kept as the place.
reason: The cells are thick-walled. The cells themselves are not thicker.
'Sepals 5': a count of 5 is right. It is stated for male flowers, but the sepal number is not sex-specific here.

target: position slot: middle to distal stem (cauline) leaves
fix: In 'Middle to distal stem leaves ...', the position words must fill the position slot. The basal leaves of this taxon have another shape (oblanceolate).
reason: Only the middle and upper stem leaves are oblong to linear. Saying this of all leaves contradicts the description of the basal leaves.
The 2-3 mm length follows the sepal description directly.
'Submembranous' leaflets: membranous with the qualifier 'approximately' is right.

fix: In Asteraceae, 'ray florets <colour>' should be annotated on the ray flower (PO_0025331), or its corolla (ligule). Do not use 'petal': the corolla is fused and the disk florets have another colour.
reason: The colour change belongs to the ray florets. 'Petal' loses the ray/disk distinction (the disk florets are yellow). The stage 'old' is right.
The lateral (female) spikes are remote, i.e. far apart. Distant, with the 'lateral' context, is right.

target: whole slot: fruit valve (the vein absence belongs to the valves)
fix: In 'valves thin, smooth, not veined', the absence of veins is limited to the part it is said of. A negated 'present' needs the whole slot, or the claim becomes 'no vascular bundles at all'.
reason: Only the fruit valves lack visible veins. Vascular bundles absent with no whole is false for the plant.

fix: In '<appressed/spreading> pubescent', the position belongs to the hairs, not to the part that carries them.
reason: The hairs are appressed to spreading. The petiole itself is not appressed or spreading.
The blade margin is rarely pinnatisect at the base. Leaf lamina base with pinnatisect and 'rarely' is right.

fix: In a feature list, 'apex X or Y' must give the apex of the current part as the bearer. The 'apex' word was dropped. Also, 'rounded' should map to the plain rounded/obtuse value, not to 'more rounded' (FLOPO_0980236), which is a comparison.
reason: Only the leaflet apex is rounded or acute, not the whole leaflet.

fix: In a feature list, 'apex X or Y' must give the apex of the current part as the bearer (leaf lamina apex = PO_0020137).
reason: Only the blade apex is acute or rounded. The blade itself is suborbicular to broadly ovate.
The scape bracts are erect. Bract erect is right; 'scape' would only narrow it.

target: towards: base of the corolla lobes (corolla lobe as the whole), not a generic base
fix: In 'adnate to base of <part>', the target is the base of that part. Keep <part> as the whole, not a bare 'plant organ base'.
reason: The filaments are fused to the base of the corolla lobes. A target of just 'base' (FLOPO_0985024) loses which organ they are fused to.
The buds are 'ovales-oblongs' (ovate-oblong). Oblong is a fair reading of this compound shape.
The inflorescences are many-flowered. Flowers present, with the count 'many', inside an inflorescence, is right.
'Sessile (or nearly so)': sessile with the qualifier 'approximately' is right.
